name: LM324DT
title: Low-power quad operational amplifiers (LM124, LM224x, LM324x)
summary: Four general-purpose bipolar op amps in one package, compensated inside and built to run from a single 3 V to 30 V supply (or ±1.5 V to ±15 V). The input range and the output both reach ground, and the four amplifiers together draw about 0.7 mA at 5 V. LM124, LM224 and LM324 differ in temperature range; A grades have tighter offset and W grades higher ESD. Packages are SO14, TSSOP14 and QFN16 3x3; LM324DT is the 0 to 70 °C standard grade in SO14.

tables.title: Absolute maximum ratings
notes: (1) Each input must stay within the supply rails, VCC+ and VCC-, in magnitude.
(2) The output current limits at about 40 mA whatever VCC is. With VCC above 15 V a short from an output to VCC can overheat the part, and shorting all four outputs together can destroy it.

(3) This current flows only while an input is pulled below ground: the input PNP transistor's base-collector diode then turns on and clamps. A parasitic NPN action on the die can at the same time push the outputs to VCC (or to ground under heavy overdrive). Nothing is damaged, and normal operation returns once the inputs are back above -0.3 V.
(4) Shorts can overheat the part; all amplifiers shorted at once can destroy it. The values are typical on a single-layer board, except TSSOP, which is measured on a two-layer board.
(5) HBM: 100 pF through 1.5 kΩ, applied between every pair of pins with the rest open.
(6) MM: 200 pF with no series resistor (source resistance below 5 Ω), applied between every pair of pins with the rest open.

circuits.title: AC coupled inverting amplifier
circuits.description: One amplifier as an inverting AC amplifier on a single supply. The signal comes in through CI and R1 to the inverting input; Rf from the output sets the gain at -Rf/R1, -10 with these values. R2 and R3 split VCC in half for the non-inverting input and C1 holds that point quiet. RB loads the output to ground, and Co passes the swing, 2 Vpp, to the load RL.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: High input Z adjustable gain DC instrumentation amplifier
circuits.description: Three amplifiers in the classic instrumentation arrangement. The two inputs drive non-inverting inputs, so both see a high impedance. R2, a 2 kΩ trimmer between the two inverting inputs, with R1 and R5 as feedback, sets the first-stage gain. The third amplifier takes the difference of the two outputs through R3, R4, R6 and R7. With R1 = R5 and R3 = R4 = R6 = R7, eo = (1 + 2R1/R2)(e2 - e1), a gain of 101 with these values.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: AC coupled non inverting amplifier
circuits.description: One amplifier as a non-inverting AC amplifier on a single supply. The signal reaches the non-inverting input through CI; R3 feeds that input its DC bias from a half-supply point made by R4 and R5 and filtered by C2. R2 from the output and R1 to C1 set the AC gain at 1 + R2/R1 (11 with these values), while C1 keeps the DC gain at one. RB loads the output and Co couples the 2 Vpp swing to RL.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: DC summing amplifier
circuits.description: One amplifier adds two inputs and subtracts two others with equal 100 kΩ resistors: e1 and e2 meet at the non-inverting input with 100 kΩ to ground, e3 and e4 meet at the inverting input with 100 kΩ feedback from the output. The result is eo = e1 + e2 - e3 - e4; on a single supply e1 + e2 must stay at or above e3 + e4 so that eo does not need to go below 0 V.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: Non-inverting DC gain
circuits.description: One amplifier with a DC gain of 1 + R2/R1, 101 with 1 MΩ and 10 kΩ. The input comes in through a 10 kΩ resistor to the non-inverting input. Its transfer plot, on a +5 V supply, rises linearly from 0 V and levels off below the 5 V rail.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: Low drift peak detector
circuits.description: A peak detector with input current compensation on its hold capacitor. Amplifier 1 charges the 1 µF capacitor through the diode and takes its feedback from the capacitor, so the capacitor keeps the highest input level. Amplifier 2, a voltage follower, buffers the held voltage to eo. The 2N929 has its collector on the hold node; amplifier 3, with R (1 MΩ) from the emitter to ground at its inverting input and 3R (3 MΩ) to ground at its non-inverting input, drives the base. The marked currents are IB out of amplifier 2's non-inverting input, 2IB in the transistor and in R, and IB at each input of amplifier 3. A 0.001 µF capacitor joins base and emitter.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: Active bandpass filter
circuits.description: A three-amplifier bandpass filter centred at 1 kHz with Q = 50 and a gain of 100 (40 dB). Amplifier 1 sums the input with feedback from the filter output through R4 (10 MΩ) and from amplifier 3 through R3, with R1 as its feedback resistor. Amplifiers 2 and 3 are integrators (R5 with C1, R6 with C2, 470 kΩ and 330 pF each); amplifier 2's output is the filter output. R7 and R8 bias the non-inverting inputs of amplifiers 2 and 3 at half of VCC, with C3 to ground.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: High input Z, DC differential amplifier
circuits.description: Two amplifiers make a differential amplifier with both inputs on non-inverting inputs. Amplifier 1 amplifies V1 by 1 + R2/R1; its output reaches amplifier 2's inverting input through R3, and amplifier 2 takes V2 at its non-inverting input with R4 as feedback. Then Vo = (1 + R4/R3)(V2 - V1), twice the difference with four 100 kΩ resistors. Common-mode rejection rests on matching R1/R2 to R4/R3.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

circuits.title: Using symmetrical amplifiers to reduce input current (general concept)
circuits.description: The general scheme of the compensation used in the peak detector. Amplifier 1 is a voltage follower from eI to eo. A 2N929 has its collector on the input node; an auxiliary amplifier, with 1.5 MΩ from the emitter to ground at its inverting input and 3 MΩ to ground at its non-inverting input, drives the base, and a 0.001 µF capacitor joins base and emitter. The marked currents are IB at each amplifier input and in the transistor path, so the input current II drawn from the source is reduced.
notes: VCC+ goes to the positive supply and VCC- to ground.

operation.text: Each device holds four independent, internally compensated high-gain amplifiers that share one pair of supply pins. The prefix gives the temperature grade: LM124 -55 to 125 °C, LM224 -40 to 105 °C, LM324 0 to 70 °C. An A suffix marks the grade with a lower input offset voltage (3 mV max at 25 °C against 5 or 7 mV); a W suffix marks the grade with a higher HBM ESD rating (700 V against 250 V).
One supply from 3 V to 30 V, or a split supply from ±1.5 V to ±15 V. The supply current is small (375 µA per amplifier) and does not depend on how large the supply voltage is.

The common-mode range reaches down to ground (the negative rail) and up to VCC+ - 1.5 V at 25 °C, VCC+ - 2 V over temperature. Neither input should go more than 0.3 V below ground; above the range, either input can go as high as 32 V without damage. The input bias current flows out of the inputs and does not change with the output's state.

With an input driven negative, the input PNP's collector-base junction conducts as a clamp diode and up to 50 mA can flow. A parasitic NPN on the die can meanwhile drive the outputs to VCC, or to ground under large overdrive. This does no harm and ends when the inputs return above -0.3 V.

The output can be shorted indefinitely; its current limits at roughly 40 mA independent of VCC, falling with temperature (about 50 mA at -55 °C to 25 mA at 125 °C). Above VCC = 15 V, a short from an output to VCC heats the part strongly, and shorts on all four amplifiers together can destroy it. The output swings low to 5 mV typical into 10 kΩ.
Channel separation is 120 dB typical from 1 kHz to 20 kHz. Coupling through stray capacitance between external parts placed close together can spoil it, mostly at higher frequencies.
The QFN16 3x3 exposed pad has no internal connection; it may be tied to VCC- or left open. Pins 3 and 10 are not connected.
Junction-to-ambient values are typical on a single-layer board for QFN16 and SO14, and on a two-layer board for TSSOP14.
